title: The Role of Kaiso as a predictive breast cancer biomarker in Africa and across the African Diaspora
text: In a rural breast cancer cohort from the South Eastern United States, the levels of the breast cancer biomarker, Kaiso in the cytoplasm, and the nucleus of breast cancer cells are each independent predictors of breast cancer survival. Surprisingly, the cytoplasmic Kaiso levels were also predictive of an immune exhausted or immune-suppressed tumor microenvironment. In this study we propose to validate these observations using 2 different breast cancer cohorts from Africa and across the African diaspora; show how these predictive linkages are influenced by patient features, genetic ancestry and exposures, tumor gene expression, tumor patterns of somatic mutation, and tumor mutational signature; and elucidate the mechanisms linking Kaiso with the breast cancer tumor microenvironment

title: Brainstem Contributions to Sensorimotor and Core Symptoms in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
text:
The prevalence and impact of autism are widely known, but the brain basis of autism remains unclear,
particularly in the understudied region of the brainstem. The proposed research will solve an urgent public
health need to provide a more complete depiction of brainstem-inclusive, whole-brain networks in reference
to the core, sensorimotor, and autonomic features prevalent in autistic children. In line with the NICHD and
IACC's priorities and with the NIH's mission, the proposed work will help promote health and well-being
through improved knowledge of the neurobiological basis of the core diagnostic and co-occurring features of
autism, enabling the development of biologically informed interventions.

title: NOLA HEAT-MAP: New Orleans Home, Environment, and Ambient Temperature: Measurements and Analysis for Preparedness
text: In the U.S., heat is responsible for more fatalities than all other weather events and Southern communities, such as New Orleans, face the highest risks. The relationship between heat and health is context-specific and local data can be used to inform heat preparedness activities. The proposed project will estimate the health burden of heat in New Orleans and identify individual and neighborhood characteristics, as well as behavior patterns, that increase vulnerability to heat.

title: Project 3: Therapeutic Gene Editing for Huntington's Disease
text: PROJECT 3 (HD) Huntington Disease (HD) is an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by the loss of striatal neurons in the central nervous system and is associated with progressive unwanted choreatic movements, behavioral and psychiatric disturbances, and dementia1,2. HD is caused by CAG triplet repeat expansions in the first exon of the HTT gene which codes for huntingtin protein, resulting in an expanded stretch of glutamines (polyQ). HD affects all ethnic groups with an average incidence of ~5 per 100,000 people, though the prevalence can vary by ~10 fold among populations. There is currently no cure or effective treatment for HD and while some therapeutic interventions may lessen the severity of patient symptoms, HD typically results in fatality within 10- 30 years of disease onset. In this follower project, we aim to improve HD protein expression to enable rescue of disease progression in HD patients. Specifically, we aim to: (1) Optimize base editing and prime editing strategies to correct HD repeat expansion; (2) Optimize AAV delivery for base and prime editor-mediated correction of the HD expansion in mice; (3) Conduct pre-clinical studies at scale (JAX). We will work closely with the Gene Editing Core to develop the latest base editing and/or prime editing technologies in HD model systems. We will iterate with the Gene Editing Core to ensure that our genome editing tools maximize on-target editing efficiencies, minimize undesirable gene editing byproducts and off-target editing events, and maximize compatibility with in vivo delivery methods of potential therapeutic relevance.

title: Understanding ApoE4-induced metabolic shifts in Alzheimer's disease
text:
ApoE4 disrupts glucose metabolism in the brain and impairs mitochondrial respiration, but we do not know why
these changes occur or how they contribute to neurodegeneration. In this proposal, we will study how ApoE4
disrupts the balance between glycolysis and respiration and produces toxic metabolites. These studies will
help us understand how ApoE4 rewires brain energy metabolism, and how this process might be targeted
therapeutically.

title: CTSA K12 Program at Baylor College of Medicine and University of Houston
text:
As part of our proposal for a “Consortium for Translational Precision Health”, this K12 program seeks to train
early-career faculty members in translational science, to help bring the benefits of scientific discoveries into
clinical practice and the health of communities. Scholars in our two-year training program, with an optional
third year, will conduct mentored research and obtain training in precision health, translational science, leader-
ship, and professional skills, aimed at developing the next generation of academic leaders.

title: Astrocyte Response to Glymphatic Shear Force
text:
The proposed studies address the issue of how forces on glial cells around blood vessels lead
to constriction or dilation of adjacent vasculature and change the fluid flow throughout the brain.
The experiments are based on our findings that astrocytes are very sensitive to flow and that
this sensitivity is amplified by concentrations of albumin that occur normally in cerebrospinal
fluid and are increased in conditions of stroke, infectious disease and autoimmunity as in
multiple sclerosis. By identifying the molecules that sense the forces on human astrocytes and
way in which their organization can be remodeled under conditions of high pressure, we expect
that we will identify new targets for therapy involving modulation of sensory functions of
astrocytes. Experiments will use a variety of techniques, including microfluidics devices,
measurement of intracellular calcium responses to diverse types of mechanical stimuli, and use
of super-resolution microscopy to identify and measure the mechanosensory complex in brains
of mice following conditions that elevate intracerebral pressure.

title: Decoding and Targeting the Molecular Mechanisms of TRAF7/KLF4 Driver Mutations in Meningioma
text:
This proposal aims to reveal the molecular mechanisms by which TRAF7 and KLF4 mutations drive meningioma
progression, filling critical gaps in the understanding of tumorigenesis and identifying potential therapeutic
targets. By leveraging innovative protein-labeling techniques and targeted therapeutic strategies, this study
seeks to uncover novel treatment avenues for these currently untreatable and often fatal brain tumors. The
findings from this research have the potential to significantly impact public health by improving treatment
outcomes, reducing tumor-associated neurological complications, and advancing precision medicine
approaches for meningioma and related disorders.

title: Hippocampal-Prefrontal Interactions Underlying Trace Memory in Aging and a Rodent Model of Alzheimer’s Disease
text:
Deficits in memory consolidation – the process through which short-term, hippocampal dependent memories
are solidified into lasting long-term memories dependent on the cortex for recall – emerge with aging and
Alzheimer’s disease. However, the neural mechanisms underlying this important cognitive process, particularly
the role of the hippocampus in instilling memory-related cortical plasticity, are poorly understood. The proposed
experiments will test hippocampal involvement in the consolidation of a hippocampal and prefrontal dependent
memory task and characterize how deficits in hippocampal-cortical communication in aging and Alzheimer’s
disease influence the induction of cortical plasticity and impair memory consolidation.

title: Multimodal AI for Monitoring and Predicting Neurocognitive Impairment in People with HIV
text:
A considerable proportion of people with HIV (PWH) still experience some form of HIV-associated
neurocognitive disorder (HAND) despite effective antiretroviral therapy, and the early detection of such
neurocognitive disorder remains challenging. Novel, data-driven multimodal approach provides opportunities
to increase robustness and accuracy of diagnostic and prognostic models by utilizing complementary
multimodal data and cutting-edge methodologies such as multimodal AI. This project aims to characterize
different biotypes of neurocognitive disorders and build multimodal AI enabled risk prediction models for
neurocognitive impairment among PWH. Personalized risk prediction through multimodal AI could improve
the predictive accuracy and early detection of neurocognitive decline in PWH and inform tailored intervention
and treatment for PWH.

title: Neurosteroids and Alcohol Use Disorder
text:
More treatment options and biomarkers for existing medications are needed for alcohol use disorder to help
patients attain their treatment goals effectively. Certain neuroactive steroids, such as allopregnanolone, that
possess properties of improving negative moods and sleep may also help relieve alcohol craving and prevent
relapse in patients with alcohol use disorder. Understanding the relationships between these endogenous
neuroactive steroids and alcohol use disorder features would add novel insights into the mechanisms and
potential biomarkers of successful treatment outcomes.

title: Satellite cells protect against pediatric chemotherapy-induced delays in muscle growth and development
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE. This research aims to improve the quality of life for childhood cancer survivors by
identifying ways to preserve muscle development and function during and after cancer treatment. The project
will evaluate how chemotherapy used to treat childhood lymphoma negatively affects skeletal muscle growth
and homeostasis throughout lifespan, and whether boosting muscle stem cells can prevent the deleterious
effects of this chemotherapy. By improving skeletal muscle growth and development, we can accelerate a child’s
return to a normal life and reduce many of the life-long comorbidities that impact childhood cancer survivors.

title: Medical Genetics Training Grant
text: Providing comprehensive research training for early-stage physician scientists in medical genetics is critical to the success of next generation leaders in medical genetics, genomics, and genetic therapies. This is center to the key NIH missions that focus on creating a skilled scientific workforce prepared to handle the increasing complexity of genomic data and developing novel genetic therapies to improve human health.

title: Using Causal Machine Learning Methods to Inform Tobacco Regulatory Science
text: This study has substantial public health relevance because it will provide rigorous evidence on the impact of e-cigarette use on subsequent combustible cigarette smoking among US youth and adults, including vulnerable populations. By leveraging causal machine learning methods, the study will inform evidence-based tobacco regulation and prevention strategies aimed at reducing nicotine addiction and the burden of smoking-related disease.

title: Pathological Inflammation Alters Oligodendrocyte Differentiation and Function
text:
Multiple sclerosis (MS) represents the most common disabling neurological disease in young adults, but
the underlying molecular mechanisms of MS remain elusive. This proposal will leverage stem cell and
genomic technologies to gain valuable insights into how changes in the function of myelinating
oligodendrocytes based on neuroinflammatory environmental cues are important in disease progression.
The results of this proposal will contribute to the development of new, exciting therapeutic approaches
for MS based on leveraging the innate regenerative capacity of oligodendrocytes.

title: Seizure frequency reduction through Bayesian-optimized cerebellar stimulation and perturbation-based risk modeling
text:
Uncontrolled seizures threaten safety, independence, and life expectancy. By advancing data-driven cerebellar
stimulation that prevents seizures and dynamical-systems probing that forecasts seizure risk, this project seeks
to transform epilepsy care from reactive treatment to proactive protection, directly advancing NIH’s mission to
reduce the burden of neurological disease.

title: Developing Experts in Computation, 'Omics and Data Exploration (DECODE) Training Program
text:
Biomedical research now produces enormous and complex datasets, but most incoming PhD students lack the
skills needed to analyze them. The DECODE program at the University of Nebraska Medical Center addresses
this gap by providing intensive training in bioinformatics, computational biology, and data science from the very
start of graduate school. Each year, six first-year and six second-year doctoral students gain experience with
real-world data projects, advanced methods such as machine learning, and professional skills in teamwork,
communication, and research integrity. By graduation, DECODE trainees will be versatile scientists equipped to
drive biomedical discovery and contribute to the nation’s data-driven research workforce.

title: Structure and Mechanism of Epigenetic Gene Silencing
text:
Gene silencing enzymes PRC1, PRC2, and DNMT1 are essential for maintaining cellular identity, and defects
in these enzymes are some of the leading causes of leukemias and cardiac diseases. We will use chemical
biology and a structure-guided approach to develop new inhibitors and activators targeting PRC2. We will use
an integrated structural and functional approach to uncover the molecular mechanisms that activate PRC1 and
DNMT1 on chromatin, which will enable the development of new therapeutic avenues targeting these enzymes.

title: Immune control of oncogene selection in preneoplastic colon
text:
Colon cancer is the fourth deadliest cancer with ~150,000 new cases and 53,000 deaths in the US in
2021. Colon cancers develop by selection of oncogenic mutations in stem cells of morphologically normal
epithelium. This proposal seeks to identify the role of immune system in suppressing selection of mutated stem
cells in the colon with the goal of developing treatment strategies to prevent colon cancers.

title: Targeting Glioblastoma Cells and Tumor Microenvironment with CAR-T Cell Therapy
text: The studies proposed herein are designed to test the feasibility, safety, and preliminary efficacy of a novel IL-13Ra2/IL-12/DR-18 CAR-T cell therapy for glioblastoma, as well as investigate response biomarkers and mechanisms of immune evasion following the injection of these CAR-T cells intratumorally and intraventricularly. We will test our hypothesis that clinically relevant CAR-T cell therapy for glioblastoma (GBM) must have two components: 1) tumor specific glioblastoma cell targeting; and 2) blockade of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We believe that our novel IL-13Ra2/IL-12/DR-18 CAR-T cell therapy that simultaneously targets both glioblastoma cells and the immunosuppressive TME may lead to improved outcomes for the treatment of glioblastoma.
